title: The tiny creatures that clean your face
titleChinese: 在你脸上 “做保洁” 的小虫子
paragraphs: What animal do we have the closest relationship with? Many people would say dogs or cats, but it's actually the tiny arachnids that live all over your face. Yes, your face. Don't worry it's probably fine. Demodex mites live in the hair follicles around the peach fuzz hair that grows on your face. They are just one of the parasites that make our bodies a habitat. Some are harmless, while there are some that can cause problems.

Demodex mites are usually harmless. They live in our pores and feed on sebum, the oil produced by our skin. This means that you find the most in the greasiest areas of your face, particularly around your eyes, nose and mouth. According to associate professor of invertebrate biology Alejandra Perotti, we should be grateful because demodex clean our pores and keep them flat. She even describes them as 'cute'. However, you can have too many of them. It is possible to find your face covered with a white frost of demodex mites. This usually only affects people if their immune system is compromised. But some people may also have an allergic reaction to these creatures.

Not all mites are as cute and useful as demodex. Scabies is a condition that is caused by mites that burrow into our skin and lay eggs. This is very itchy and usually spreads to most of a person's body. It can also be quite uncomfortable to think about and is often stigmatised. Now, this is a problem because it can delay people getting treatment. Some of this stigma can come because we often associate scabies with people being unclean. This, however, is a complete myth.

This stigma may also be linked to how we feel. Mites and other parasites often cause us to feel disgust. This is something that we may have evolved to help us avoid illnesses, but here it could be stopping people getting the help they need or causing us to worry about something that can even be beneficial.
chineseParagraphs: 我们与哪种动物的关系最密切？很多人可能会说是狗或猫，但实际上，是生活在你全脸的小型蛛形纲动物。是的，你的脸。别担心，通常没问题。蠕形螨生活在您脸上桃红色绒毛周围的毛囊里。它们只是将我们身体当作栖息地的寄生虫之一。有些无害，而有些则可能引起问题。

蠕形螨通常无害。它们生活在我们的毛孔中，以皮脂（皮肤产生的油脂）为食。这意味着它们在你脸上最油的区域最多，尤其是眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴周围。据无脊椎生物学副教授亚历杭德拉·佩罗蒂称，我们应该心存感激，因为蠕形螨清洁我们的毛孔并使其保持平整。她甚至形容它们“可爱”。然而，你可能会有过多的蠕形螨。你可能会发现你的脸上覆盖着一层白色的“霜”，那其实是蠕形螨。这通常只影响免疫系统受损的人。但有些人也可能对这些生物产生过敏反应。
并非所有螨虫都像蠕形螨一样可爱有用。疥疮是由钻入我们皮肤并产卵的螨虫引起的一种疾病。这非常痒，通常会蔓延到人的大部分身体。一想到这种情况人们会有不适的感觉，并且常常感觉很羞耻。现在，这是一个问题，因为它可能会延误人们接受治疗。这种羞耻部分源于我们常将疥疮与人不洁联系在一起。然而，这完全是一种误解。
这种羞耻也可能与我们自身的感受有关。螨虫和其他寄生虫常常让我们感到恶心。这种反应可能是我们在进化过程中形成的，以帮助我们避免疾病，但在这种情况下，它却可能阻止人们获得所需的帮助，或让我们对某些甚至可能有益的东西感到担忧。

vocabulary.definition: 蛛形纲动物（动物学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: arachnid /əˈræknɪd/ n. 蛛形纲动物（动物学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Spiders and scorpions are arachnids.
vocabulary.translation: 蜘蛛和蝎子都是蛛形纲动物。

vocabulary.definition: 蠕形螨（生物学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: demodex mite /ˈdemədeks maɪt/ n. 蠕形螨（生物学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Demodex mites are microscopic creatures that live on human skin.
vocabulary.translation: 蠕形螨是生活在人类皮肤上的微小生物。

vocabulary.entry: hair follicle /ˈheə ˌfɒlɪkl/ n. 毛囊（解剖学术语）
vocabulary.example: Hair grows from hair follicles in the skin.
vocabulary.translation: 头发从皮肤中的毛囊生长出来。

vocabulary.entry: peach fuzz /ˌpiːtʃ ˈfʌz/ n. 细软茸毛（口语）
vocabulary.example: She has soft peach fuzz on her cheeks.
vocabulary.translation: 她脸颊上有柔软的细毛。

vocabulary.definition: 寄生虫（生物学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: parasite /ˈpærəsaɪt/ n. 寄生虫（生物学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Fleas and ticks are common parasites on dogs.
vocabulary.translation: 跳蚤和蜱虫是狗身上常见的寄生虫。

vocabulary.definition: 栖息地（生态学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: habitat /ˈhæbɪtæt/ n. 栖息地（生态学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The forest provides a habitat for many species.
vocabulary.translation: 这片森林为许多物种提供了栖息地。

vocabulary.entry: pore /pɔː(r)/ n. 毛孔
vocabulary.example: Sweat comes out of the pores in your skin.
vocabulary.translation: 汗液从皮肤的毛孔中排出。

vocabulary.entry: sebum /ˈsiːbəm/ n. 皮脂（生理学术语）
vocabulary.example: Sebum is an oily substance produced by the skin.
vocabulary.translation: 皮脂是皮肤产生的一种油性物质。

vocabulary.entry: greasy /ˈɡriːsi/ adj. 油腻的，油性的
vocabulary.example: Her skin was greasy and she needed to wash her face.
vocabulary.translation: 她的皮肤很油，需要洗脸。

vocabulary.entry: associate professor /əˈsəʊsieɪt prəˈfesə(r)/ n. 副教授
vocabulary.example: She was promoted to associate professor last year.
vocabulary.translation: 她去年被提升为副教授。

vocabulary.definition: 无脊椎动物（动物学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: invertebrate /ɪnˈvɜːtɪbrət/ n. 无脊椎动物（动物学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Insects and worms are invertebrates.
vocabulary.translation: 昆虫和蠕虫都是无脊椎动物。

vocabulary.entry: immune system /ɪˈmjuːn ˌsɪstəm/ n. 免疫系统（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: A healthy diet can help strengthen your immune system.
vocabulary.translation: 健康饮食有助于增强免疫系统。

vocabulary.entry: compromised /ˈkɒmprəmaɪzd/ adj. 削弱的，受损的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: People with compromised immune systems are more vulnerable to infection.
vocabulary.translation: 免疫系统受损的人更容易受到感染。

vocabulary.definition: 过敏反应（医学术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: allergic reaction /əˌlɜːdʒɪk riˈækʃn/ n. 过敏反应（医学术语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She had a severe allergic reaction to peanuts.
vocabulary.translation: 她对花生有严重的过敏反应。

vocabulary.entry: scabies /ˈskeɪbiːz/ n. 疥疮（医学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Scabies is caused by tiny mites that burrow into the skin.
vocabulary.translation: 疥疮是由钻入皮肤的小螨虫引起的。

vocabulary.entry: burrow /ˈbʌrəʊ/ v. 挖洞，钻入（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Rabbits burrow underground to make their homes.
vocabulary.translation: 兔子在地下挖洞筑巢。

vocabulary.entry: itchy /ˈɪtʃi/ adj. 发痒的
vocabulary.example: The insect bite was red and itchy.
vocabulary.translation: 蚊虫叮咬处又红又痒。

vocabulary.entry: stigmatised /ˈstɪɡmətaɪzd/ adj. 被污名化的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Mental illness is often stigmatised in society.
vocabulary.translation: 精神疾病在社会上常常被污名化。

vocabulary.entry: associate /əˈsəʊsieɪt/ v. 联系，联想（书面语）
vocabulary.example: People often associate walking with leisure.
vocabulary.translation: 人们常将步行与休闲联系在一起。

vocabulary.entry: unclean /ʌnˈkliːn/ adj. 不洁的，肮脏的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The unclean conditions in the kitchen caused health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 厨房的不洁条件导致了健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: myth /mɪθ/ n. 误解，虚构的观念
vocabulary.example: It's a myth that older people can't learn new skills.
vocabulary.translation: 年长者学不会新技能是一种误解。

vocabulary.entry: disgust /dɪsˈɡʌst/ n. 恶心，厌恶（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The smell of rotten meat filled her with disgust.
vocabulary.translation: 腐肉的气味让她充满厌恶。

vocabulary.entry: evolve /iˈvɒlv/ v. 进化，演变（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The company has evolved from a small family business.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司是从一个小型家族企业演变而来的。

vocabulary.entry: beneficial /ˌbenɪˈfɪʃl/ adj. 有益的，有利的
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is beneficial to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼对你的健康有益。
